newsitem.title: CHINA: China warns France over Dalai Lama visit.
newsitem.headline: China warns France over Dalai Lama visit.

text.p: China warned Paris on Friday that its relations with Beijing would suffer if French officials met Tibet's exiled god-king the Dalai Lama during his visit to France.
"We still hope the French side...will not have any form of official relations with the Dalai Lama," Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang told a regular news briefing.
"Otherwise, Sino-French relations will be damaged," Shen said.

Shen said Paris had given assurances to Beijing that French officials would not meet the Dalai Lama, who fled Tibet in 1959 after a failed uprising against Chinese rule and won the Nobel Peace prize in 1989 for his peaceful campaign for autonomy in his homeland.
Beijing accuses him of campaigning for Tibetan independence.

"The French side indicated the Dalai Lama would be in touch only with non-governmental persons on his visit to France and that French officials will not have any contacts with the Dalai Lama," Shen said.
The globe-trotting Buddhist monk, on a two-day visit to France, accused China on Tuesday of committing "cultural genocide" in Tibet.
"A kind of cultural genocide is taking place in Tibet" the Dalai Lama told French daily Le Monde in an interview.
"Losing one's independence is acceptable, but losing one's culture, accepting the destruction of our spiritualism, of Tibetan Buddhism, is unthinkable," he said.
The Dalai Lama has long insisted he is not seeking to split Tibet from the rest of China.
Shen dismissed such pledges as insincere and deceptive.
"The Dalai Lama has never officially showed us that he has given up the stance of Tibetan independence," Shen said.
"What he spreads in foreign countries, that he does not seek Tibetan independence, deceives public opinion and deceives Western governments," Shen said.
China last week labelled as "rude interference" in its internal affairs a meeting between the Dalai Lama and officials from the European Parliament during the god-king's current European tour.
Beijing threatened possible trade retaliation against Canberra after a meeting between the Dalai Lama and Australian Prime Minister John Howard last month.

The Dalai Lama is scheduled to meet French parliamentarians, Socialist opposition leader Lionel Jospin and Paris mayor Jean Tiberi during his stay in the French capital, but no official meeting is planned with government representatives.
